from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Racing Paradox"
        lines = [
            "Which path gets a marble from A to B fastest?",
            "A straight line is the shortest distance.",
            "But is it the fastest path?",
            "Let's race marbles on different curves.",
            "Surprisingly, the straight line loses the race."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display Point A and Point B with labels (#FFFFFF).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        point_a = Dot(color=WHITE)
        point_b = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(point_a, 'B1')
        self.place_at_grid(point_b, 'E5')
        
        label_a = MathTex("A", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        label_b = MathTex("B", color=WHITE).scale(0.8)
        label_a.next_to(point_a, UP)
        label_b.next_to(point_b, DOWN)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point_a), FadeIn(point_b), Write(label_a), Write(label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Draw three paths: Straight Line (#FF4444)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4444")
        
        start_pos = self.grid['B1']
        end_pos = self.grid['E5']
        
        straight_path = Line(start_pos, end_pos, color="#FF4444")
        
        self.play(Create(straight_path))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Deep Curve (#44FF44), and Steepest Curve (#4444FF).
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE) # Neutral/General question
        
        # Deep Curve (Parabolic-ish)
        # We'll use a CubicBezier to approximate
        deep_path = CubicBezier(
            start_pos,
            start_pos + DOWN * 2,
            end_pos + LEFT * 1,
            end_pos,
            color="#44FF44"
        )
        
        # Steepest Curve (Cycloid-ish)
        # Brachistochrone is very steep at the start
        steep_path = CubicBezier(
            start_pos,
            start_pos + DOWN * 4,
            end_pos + LEFT * 0.5,
            end_pos,
            color="#4444FF"
        )
        
        self.play(Create(deep_path), Create(steep_path))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Start the race: Marbles (#FFFFFF) traverse the paths at different speeds.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        
        marble_red = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(start_pos)
        marble_green = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(start_pos)
        marble_blue = Dot(color=WHITE).move_to(start_pos)
        
        self.add(marble_red, marble_green, marble_blue)
        
        # We want Blue to win, then Green, then Red.
        # Blue (Steepest) path is the fastest descent.
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(marble_blue, steep_path, rate_func=linear, run_time=2.0),
            MoveAlongPath(marble_green, deep_path, rate_func=linear, run_time=2.5),
            MoveAlongPath(marble_red, straight_path, rate_func=linear, run_time=3.5),
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlight the Steepest Curve (#4444FF) as it finishes first.
        # Surprisingly, the straight line loses the race.
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#4444FF")
        
        self.play(
            steep_path.animate.set_stroke(width=8),
            marble_blue.animate.scale(1.5),
            Indicate(self.lecture[4])
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup layout
        title_text = "Prerequisite Knowledge: The Speed-Height Relationship"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Velocity depends on the vertical distance dropped.",
            "Energy conservation dictates speed increases with depth.",
            "A steeper initial drop grants higher velocity early."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Colors
        COLOR_FORMULA = "#FFFF00"  # bright yellow
        COLOR_VECTOR = "#00FFFF"   # cyan
        COLOR_SPEEDO = "#FFA500"   # orange
        
        # Constants for physics
        g = 9.8
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Velocity depends on the vertical distance dropped."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_FORMULA))
        
        formula = MathTex("v = \\sqrt{2gy}", color=COLOR_FORMULA)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Energy conservation dictates speed increases with depth."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_VECTOR)
        )
        
        # Visual setup for falling block
        # Start and end points for the fall
        start_pos = self.grid["C3"].copy()
        end_pos = self.grid["E3"].copy()
        dist = start_pos[1] - end_pos[1]
        
        block = Square(side_length=0.4, fill_opacity=1, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(block, "C3")
        
        y_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        block.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(start_pos + DOWN * y_tracker.get_value()))
        
        # Velocity vector that grows with the block (v = sqrt(2gy))
        moving_vector = always_redraw(lambda: Vector(
            DOWN * (np.sqrt(2 * g * y_tracker.get_value()) * 0.2 + 0.1),
            color=COLOR_VECTOR
        ).move_to(block.get_center(), aligned_edge=UP))
        
        trail_vectors = VGroup()
        self.add(block, moving_vector, trail_vectors)
        
        # Animation: Fall to demonstrate speed increasing with depth
        self.play(
            y_tracker.animate.set_value(dist),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_quad # Simple acceleration simulation
        )
        
        # Add trail static vectors at fixed height intervals
        for y_v in [0.4, 0.8, 1.2, 1.6]:
            if y_v < dist:
                v_mag = np.sqrt(2 * g * y_v) * 0.2 + 0.1
                v_static = Vector(DOWN * v_mag, color=COLOR_VECTOR, stroke_opacity=0.4)
                v_static.move_to(start_pos + DOWN * y_v, aligned_edge=UP)
                trail_vectors.add(v_static)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "A steeper initial drop grants higher velocity early."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_SPEEDO)
        )
        
        # Speedometer setup
        gauge = Arc(radius=0.7, start_angle=PI, angle=-PI, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(gauge, "D6") # Offset to maintain clear corridor for falling block
        gauge_line = Line(gauge.get_start(), gauge.get_end(), color=WHITE)
        
        # Needle rotation based on velocity ratio
        needle = Line(gauge.get_center(), gauge.get_center() + LEFT * 0.6, color=COLOR_SPEEDO)
        needle.set_stroke(width=4)
        
        speed_label = Text("Speed", font_size=16, color=COLOR_SPEEDO)
        speed_label.next_to(gauge, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        speedo = VGroup(gauge, gauge_line, needle, speed_label)
        
        def update_needle(m):
            y_val = y_tracker.get_value()
            v_val = np.sqrt(2 * g * y_val)
            v_max = np.sqrt(2 * g * dist)
            ratio = v_val / v_max if v_max > 0 else 0
            angle = PI * (1 - ratio) # Needle moves from PI (left) to 0 (right)
            
            center = gauge.get_center()
            end = center + np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0]) * 0.6
            m.put_start_and_end_on(center, end)
            
        needle.add_updater(update_needle)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(speedo))
        
        # Reset and run again to show synchronization between block fall and speedometer
        self.play(y_tracker.animate.set_value(0), run_time=1)
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(
            y_tracker.animate.set_value(dist),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_quad
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Knowledge: Snell's Law and Light", 
                         ["Light always follows the path of least time.", 
                          "Snell's Law describes how light bends between media.", 
                          "Light curves to spend more time in faster zones."])

        # Colors for elements
        ray_color = "#FFFFFF"
        snell_color = "#FFFF00"
        layer_color = "#888888"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(ray_color))
        
        # Setup the interface and normal for Snell's Law
        # Interface is between Row C and Row D
        y_c = self.grid["C3"][1]
        y_d = self.grid["D3"][1]
        interface_y = (y_c + y_d) / 2
        
        # Normal line at the center of the visual area (between Col 3 and 4)
        x_normal = (self.grid["C3"][0] + self.grid["C4"][0]) / 2
        
        interface = Line(start=[0.5, interface_y, 0], end=[5.5, interface_y, 0], color=GRAY)
        normal = DashedLine(start=[x_normal, 2.5, 0], end=[x_normal, -2.8, 0], color=GRAY_A)
        
        # Light ray starting from A1, hitting interface at normal, and entering second medium
        p_start = self.grid["B1"]
        p_hit = np.array([x_normal, interface_y, 0])
        p_end = self.grid["E5"]
        
        ray_part1 = Line(p_start, p_hit, color=ray_color)
        ray_part2 = Line(p_hit, p_end, color=ray_color)
        
        self.play(Create(interface), Create(normal))
        self.play(Create(ray_part1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight second lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(snell_color))
        
        # Show bending ray
        self.play(Create(ray_part2))
        
        # Angles and formula
        # Incident angle theta1
        arc1 = Arc(start_angle=-PI/2, angle=ray_part1.get_angle() + PI/2, radius=0.4, arc_center=p_hit, color=snell_color)
        theta1 = MathTex(r"\theta_1", color=snell_color, font_size=24)
        theta1.move_to(p_hit + UP * 0.6 + LEFT * 0.4)
        
        # Refracted angle theta2
        arc2 = Arc(start_angle=-PI/2, angle=ray_part2.get_angle() + PI/2, radius=0.4, arc_center=p_hit, color=snell_color)
        theta2 = MathTex(r"\theta_2", color=snell_color, font_size=24)
        theta2.move_to(p_hit + DOWN * 0.6 + RIGHT * 0.4)
        
        # Snell's Law equation - positioned in top right area
        snell_eq = MathTex(r"n_1 \sin \theta_1 = n_2 \sin \theta_2", color=snell_color, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(snell_eq, "A3", "A6")
        
        self.play(Create(arc1), Write(theta1))
        self.play(Create(arc2), Write(theta2))
        self.play(Write(snell_eq))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight third lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(layer_color))
        
        # Transition out Snell's Law setup
        self.play(
            FadeOut(ray_part1), FadeOut(ray_part2), FadeOut(interface), FadeOut(normal),
            FadeOut(arc1), FadeOut(theta1), FadeOut(arc2), FadeOut(theta2), FadeOut(snell_eq)
        )
        
        # Simulate layered media with decreasing refractive indices
        layers = VGroup()
        for i, row in enumerate(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]):
            rect = Rectangle(height=1.0, width=5.0, color=layer_color, stroke_width=1)
            rect.set_fill(layer_color, opacity=0.05 * (i + 1))
            self.place_in_area(rect, f"{row}1", f"{row}6")
            layers.add(rect)
            
        self.play(Create(layers))
        
        # Animate curved ray (bending toward horizontal to minimize time in lower-v/higher-n zones?)
        # "Light curves to spend more time in faster zones." 
        # If speed increases with depth (decreasing n), the ray flattens out.
        path_pts = [
            self.grid["A2"],
            self.grid["B2"] + RIGHT * 0.2,
            self.grid["C3"],
            self.grid["D4"] + RIGHT * 0.3,
            self.grid["E5"] + RIGHT * 0.4,
            self.grid["F6"]
        ]
        curved_ray = VMobject(color=ray_color)
        curved_ray.set_points_as_corners(path_pts)
        curved_ray.make_smooth()
        
        self.play(Create(curved_ray), run_time=3)
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The 'Aha!' Moment: Mechanical Light", [
            "Imagine the vertical space as many thin layers.",
            "The marble speeds up as it crosses each layer.",
            "This is exactly how light behaves in varying media.",
            "The fastest descent follows the path of light.",
            "This link reveals the optimal descent curve."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Layer lines - color #333333
        layers = VGroup(*[
            Line(self.grid[f"{row}1"] + LEFT*0.5, self.grid[f"{row}6"] + RIGHT*0.5, color="#333333", stroke_width=2)
            for row in ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        ])
        # Add a final bottom boundary for the last layer
        layers.add(Line(self.grid["F1"] + LEFT*0.5 + DOWN*1.0, self.grid["F6"] + RIGHT*0.5 + DOWN*1.0, color="#333333", stroke_width=2))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#333333"))
        self.play(Create(layers), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Segmented path points to simulate refraction-like steps
        path_points = [
            self.grid["A1"],
            self.grid["B2"],
            self.grid["C3"],
            self.grid["D4"],
            self.grid["E5"],
            self.grid["F6"]
        ]
        
        segments = VGroup()
        for i in range(len(path_points) - 1):
            segments.add(Line(path_points[i], path_points[i+1], color="#00FF00", stroke_width=4))
        
        marble = Dot(path_points[0], color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.add(marble)
        self.play(Create(segments), run_time=2)
        
        # Marble acceleration: duration for each segment decreases
        for i in range(len(path_points) - 1):
            segment_time = 0.8 * (0.7**i)
            self.play(marble.animate.move_to(path_points[i+1]), run_time=segment_time, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(marble))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Labeling speeds to emphasize the analogy with light (refractive index)
        v_labels = VGroup()
        for i, row in enumerate(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]):
            label = MathTex(f"v_{i+1}", color="#00FF00", font_size=24)
            self.place_at_grid(label, f"{row}1")
            label.shift(LEFT * 0.4 + UP * 0.3)
            v_labels.add(label)
            
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Write(v_labels))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Morph segmented path to a smooth curve (Descent follows path of light)
        # Using a smooth curve through the refraction points
        smooth_curve = VMobject(color="#FF00FF", stroke_width=4)
        smooth_curve.set_points_as_corners(path_points).make_smooth()
        
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(
            FadeOut(v_labels),
            Transform(segments, smooth_curve)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Final optimal descent curve
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(segments.animate.set_stroke(width=8), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(segments.animate.set_stroke(width=4), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(2)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the scene
        title = "The Solution: The Cycloid"
        lines = [
            "This optimal path is called a cycloid.",
            "A cycloid is traced by a point on a rolling wheel.",
            "It perfectly balances high speed and short distance.",
            "Mathematics proves the cycloid is the fastest."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Define colors
        color_path = "#00FFFF"
        color_wheel = "#CCCCCC"
        color_dot = "#FF0000"
        color_label = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "This optimal path is called a cycloid."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_label), run_time=0.5)
        
        # Show "Cycloid" label in the grid area initially
        label = Text("Cycloid", color=color_label)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "A cycloid is traced by a point on a rolling wheel."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_wheel),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        # Wheel parameters
        radius = 0.5
        # Define wheel at start (Left side of grid)
        # Using row E as the floor
        start_center = self.grid["E1"] + UP * radius
        end_center = self.grid["E6"] + UP * radius

        wheel = Circle(radius=radius, color=color_wheel)
        wheel.move_to(start_center)
        
        dot = Dot(color=color_dot).scale(1.2)
        # Position dot at the bottom of the wheel initially
        dot.move_to(wheel.get_bottom())

        wheel_group = VGroup(wheel, dot)
        
        # Line for the ground
        ground = Line(self.grid["F1"], self.grid["F6"], color=GREY_E)
        
        self.play(Create(ground), Create(wheel), FadeIn(dot))
        
        # Tracer for the cycloid
        path_tracker = TracedPath(dot.get_center, stroke_color=color_path, stroke_width=4)
        self.add(path_tracker)

        # Roller animation using ValueTracker for rotation/translation
        # Angle t goes from 0 to 2*pi
        roll_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        def update_wheel(mob):
            t = roll_tracker.get_value()
            # Distance rolled is r * t
            dist = radius * t
            mob.move_to(start_center + RIGHT * dist)
            
        def update_dot(mob):
            t = roll_tracker.get_value()
            dist = radius * t
            center = start_center + RIGHT * dist
            # Dot position relative to center: ( -r*sin(t), -r*cos(t) )
            # at t=0, it's at (0, -r) -> bottom
            offset = np.array([-radius * np.sin(t), -radius * np.cos(t), 0])
            mob.move_to(center + offset)

        wheel.add_updater(update_wheel)
        dot.add_updater(update_dot)

        # Calculate max t to reach E6
        total_dist = (self.grid["E6"][0] - self.grid["E1"][0])
        max_t = total_dist / radius

        self.play(roll_tracker.animate.set_value(max_t), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        
        wheel.remove_updater(update_wheel)
        dot.remove_updater(update_dot)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "It perfectly balances high speed and short distance."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_path),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # Highlight the path
        self.play(path_tracker.animate.set_stroke(width=8), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(path_tracker.animate.set_stroke(width=4), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Mathematics proves the cycloid is the fastest."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GOLD),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # Let's move the label to be more prominent above the peak.
        self.play(
            label.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"] + RIGHT * 0.5),
            wheel_group.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            run_time=1
        )

        self.wait(2)

        # Cleanup for next section
        self.play(
            FadeOut(label),
            FadeOut(wheel_group),
            FadeOut(path_tracker),
            FadeOut(ground),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE)
        )

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        # Calculate center of the area

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Tautochrone Property & Real-world Application"
        lines = [
            "The cycloid is also a tautochrone curve.",
            "Objects released from any height finish together.",
            "This property is used in clocks and engineering."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        GREEN_RAMP = "#00FF00"
        RED_MARBLE = "#FF0000"
        BLUE_MARBLE = "#0000FF"
        WHITE_MARBLE = "#FFFFFF"
        FLASH_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The cycloid is also a tautochrone curve."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GREEN_RAMP))
        
        # Cycloid ramp parameters
        r = 0.55
        # x = r(t - sin t), y = -r(1 - cos t)
        def ramp_func(t):
            # t from 0 to PI
            # t=0: top-left (0,0)
            # t=PI: bottom-right (PI*r, -2r)
            return np.array([r * (t - np.sin(t)), -r * (1 - np.cos(t)), 0])

        ramp = ParametricFunction(ramp_func, t_range=[0, PI], color=GREEN_RAMP)
        # Shift and place
        self.place_in_area(ramp, "B1", "E5")
        
        self.play(Create(ramp))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Objects released from any height finish together."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # Marbles at different heights (proportions along the curve)
        # Proportion 0 is top, 1 is bottom (t=PI)
        props = [0.15, 0.45, 0.75]
        marbles = VGroup(
            Dot(color=RED_MARBLE, radius=0.12),
            Dot(color=BLUE_MARBLE, radius=0.12),
            Dot(color=WHITE_MARBLE, radius=0.12)
        )
        
        # Initial positions
        for i, m in enumerate(marbles):
            m.move_to(ramp.point_from_proportion(props[i]))
            
        self.play(FadeIn(marbles))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Slide animation: all marbles reach the end (proportion 1.0) simultaneously
        def slide_animation(mobject, start_prop):
            return UpdateFromAlphaFunc(
                mobject,
                lambda m, alpha: m.move_to(
                    ramp.point_from_proportion(interpolate(start_prop, 1.0, alpha))
                )
            )

        self.play(
            slide_animation(marbles[0], props[0]),
            slide_animation(marbles[1], props[1]),
            slide_animation(marbles[2], props[2]),
            run_time=2.5,
            rate_func=bezier([0.4, 0, 1, 1]) # Accelerating start
        )

        # Simultaneous collision flash at the bottom
        flash = Flash(ramp.get_end(), color=FLASH_COLOR, line_length=0.4, num_lines=12, flash_radius=0.3)
        self.play(flash)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "This property is used in clocks and engineering."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE_MARBLE))
        
        # Subtle emphasis: have marbles pulse or settle
        self.play(
            *[m.animate.scale(1.2).set_opacity(0.8) for m in marbles],
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            *[m.animate.scale(1/1.2).set_opacity(0.6) for m in marbles],
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Brachistochrone Problem: The Path of Fastest Descent
outline.target_audience: Senior High School or First-year University Students (Physics/Calculus interest)

sections.title: The Racing Paradox
sections.content: Introduce the challenge: If a marble needs to travel from Point A to Point B (lower and offset) under gravity, which path is the fastest? Contrast three paths: a straight line (the shortest distance), a circular arc, and a steep curve that flattens out. Challenge the audience's intuition that 'shortest distance' equals 'shortest time'.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Race of Three Marbles': An animation shows a red marble on a straight ramp, a blue marble on a deep curve, and a green marble on a cycloid. The straight line surprisingly loses.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: The Speed-Height Relationship
sections.content: Establish the physics of the problem using the Conservation of Energy ($mgh = 1/2 mv^2$). Explain that the velocity ($v$) at any point depends solely on the vertical distance dropped ($y$). More drop early on means higher velocity for the rest of the trip.
sections.example: A 'Speedometer' graphic appears next to a falling object: As $y$ increases, the vector $v = \sqrt{2gy}$ grows proportionally. This explains why a steeper drop at the start is beneficial.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Snell's Law and Light
sections.content: Introduce Fermat's Principle: Light always takes the path of least time. Review Snell's Law ($n_1 \sin \theta_1 = n_2 \sin \theta_2$). Explain that in a medium where speed changes (refractive index varies), light bends to optimize its travel time.
sections.example: A laser beam passing through layers of water with different salt concentrations. The beam doesn't travel in a straight line; it curves to spend more time in 'fast' zones.

sections.title: The 'Aha!' Moment: Mechanical Light
sections.content: Bridge the gap between a falling marble and a light ray. Imagine the vertical space divided into infinite horizontal layers. As the marble falls, its speed increases in each layer, just like light entering a medium with a lower refractive index. To minimize time, the marble must follow the same path light would take through these layers.
sections.example: An animation showing a marble's trajectory being modeled as a series of refracted light segments, gradually smoothing into a continuous curve.

sections.title: The Solution: The Cycloid
sections.content: Identify the resulting curve as a 'Cycloid'. Define a cycloid as the path traced by a point on the rim of a rolling wheel. Explain its unique property: it is the perfect mathematical balance between gaining speed quickly (steepness) and minimizing distance.
sections.example: A glowing dot on a bicycle wheel rim traces a red curve on a wall as the bike moves forward. This 'rolling' geometry is the same curve that wins the race.

sections.title: The Tautochrone Property & Real-world Application
sections.content: Reveal the 'Tautochrone' (same time) property: No matter where you release the marble on a cycloid curve, it will reach the bottom in the exact same amount of time. Conclude with applications in engineering and slide design.
sections.example: A 'Multi-Marble Race': Three marbles are released from different heights on the same cycloid ramp. They all collide at the bottom at the exact same millisecond. End with a shot of a professional skate park 'half-pipe' reflecting these curves.
